architecture_delta.name: LOST_ACK_DURABLE_RETURN_CAUSAL_REENTRY_FALSIFIER
architecture_delta.reason: Individual WP103/WP104/WP105 components encode the desired separations, but current evidence does not prove their integrated behavior under an ambiguous/lost acknowledgement recovery path.
required_trace: OFFER attempt B with a fresh transport_attempt_id but unchanged logical delivery/result identity
ACK bound to an actually offered attempt
ACK changes delivery state only and does not itself prove parent consumption
parent causal re-entry uses a fresh resume.causal_id and strictly later generation while preserving exact bound child result digest
no delivery/retry transition may mint effect success, task completion, or whole-system completion
if any external effect outcome is UNKNOWN, recovery may verify but may not blindly replay the effect
architecture_delta.acceptance_shape: canonical F2-WP-004 run package around a deterministic repository-hosted integration test; source/CI evidence first, runtime credit remains zero until a later admitted target-runtime gate

counterhypothesis_result: The counterhypothesis is largely correct: F2 already implements most useful Temporal-style separation. The novel value is an integrated lost-ack falsifier, not a new subsystem.
expected_information_gain: HIGH because a failure would reveal cross-layer authority leakage despite individually green components; a pass would close a concrete integration gap without adding a second state/effect authority.
